extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, stakeholders, and organizations submitting comments to CFPB notices and rulemaking dockets
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and submitting public comments to CFPB notices and Notices of Proposed Rulemaking, covering where notices are posted, submission options and timing, public record implications, exceptions, privacy precautions, and how comments are used in rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting and access of notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Bureau notices open for public comment are posted to the Notice and Opportunities to Comment section when publicly released, which may precede Federal Register publication by days to weeks. All notices requesting comment and published in the Federal Register receive dockets on Regulations.gov, typically opened on the publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect notices to appear on the CFPB site when publicly released and on Regulations.gov when published in the Federal Register; timing may differ and postings on CFPB can precede the official Federal Register publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred submission timing and alternate submission methods
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notice has been released but not yet published in the Federal Register, commenters can either wait for the official version (which is preferred) or submit comments through alternate means listed in the notice's ADDRESSES section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible, submit to the official Federal Register/Regulations.gov docket; only use alternate submission routes listed in the notice's ADDRESSES if you need to comment before the Federal Register version is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public record policy (comments posted and disclosed)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Bureau currently has a policy of generally posting all comments received (by any means specified in the notice) to the docket on Regulations.gov." All comments, attachments, and supporting materials become part of the public record subject to disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume submissions (including attachments and supporting materials) will be posted and discoverable; there is generally no independent verification or routine redaction by the Bureau before posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to posting
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bureau may decline to post or withdraw certain materials, including duplicate submissions, copyrighted content not owned by the submitter, confidential business information, spam, threats, and disavowed comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid submitting content that is copyrighted by others, contains confidential business information, or could be construed as spam or threats; duplicates and disavowed comments may be removed or withheld from the docket.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy caution for commenters
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters should avoid including proprietary information, sensitive personal data (like account or Social Security numbers), or other individuals' names, as the Bureau generally posts all comments without independent verification or standard redaction of identifying information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redact or omit sensitive personal or proprietary details before submission; do not rely on the Bureau to redact identifying information from posted comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of comments in rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bureau uses public comments submitted in response to Notices of Proposed Rulemaking to inform decision-making by considering their substantive content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus comments on substantive, well-supported points relevant to the notice, because the Bureau weighs the substantive content of submissions when informing rulemaking decisions.
